newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portuguese labour laws not rigid - minister.
newsitem.headline: Portuguese labour laws not rigid - minister.

text.p: Portugal's labour laws are no more rigid than elsewhere in the European Union and the government was taking steps to help firms restructure their workforces when needed, Employment Minister Maria Joao Rodrigues said.
Portuguese business leaders have criticised labour laws, saying they made it hard for companies to dismiss workers.
"The dismissals law in Portugal is similar to that in most of the rest of the EU countries," Rodrigues told Reuters in an interview on Friday night.
"Sometimes there is a difficulty in applying the law because a Portuguese company cannot pay the employee the compensation owed to him when he is dismissed," she added.

She said that under the terms of an agreement reached between the government, unions and companies, a fund would be set up to pay compensation to workers who were dismissed by companies that were restructuring to adapt to market conditions.
The state and the companies concerned would finance the fund, she added. She gave no further details.
